reader.requirement: At 85 each record of an indexed file is identified by its key values: a random READ by the prime key or (level 2) an alternate key returns the record holding that value ('02' when a duplicate alternate follows), an absent value is '23', a duplicate prime key on WRITE is '22', and sequential access follows the key of reference, for fixed and RECORD VARYING records.

edition-consulted.switches: no switch on the key lookup; DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly (line 580) decides when '02' is reported, another rule's detail

reader.edition-search: grep DialectBehaviors in IndexedConnector.cs, KeyedStore.cs, KeyedConnector.cs: two consults, both READ status or positioning details; none on how a record is identified by its key.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for identification by key; the '02' reporting rule has an edition arm that belongs to the READ rules
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness reads one prime key and one absent key; not exercised: alternate keys with duplicates, key-order sequential access, a duplicate prime WRITE, variable-length records

reader.notes: Identification by key is the keyed store's lookup, shared by every edition; the probes cover prime and alternate keys, duplicates and variable-length records at --std 85.
